chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Amr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The best of your dates is Al-Barni; it removes the illness and there is no illness in it, and it removes the fatigue and there is no harm for it, and it removes the phlegm; and with every date is a good deed (reward).
And in another report: It is palatable and wholesome, and it removes the fatigue, and it satiates.

key_terms.الْبَرْنِيُّ: A specific variety of dates known for its quality and medicinal properties.
key_terms.يَهْنَأُ: It is palatable or pleasing to eat.

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits and spiritual rewards of eating Al-Barni dates according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the Barni date variety for its comprehensive therapeutic profile, noting its ability to dispel illness, fatigue, and phlegm without adverse effects, thereby embodying the Prophetic tradition of food as medicine. The narration further links physical sustenance with spiritual merit, asserting that each date consumed carries a good deed, while an alternative report underscores its palatability and satiating quality. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integration of bodily health and spiritual reward through natural, sunnah-compliant foods.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Abu Amro, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The best of your dates is Al-Barny, it does away with the illnesses, and there is no illness in it, and it does away with the fatigue and there is no harmfulness for it, and it does away with the phlegm; and with every date is a Reward’.
And in another report, ‘It is palatable, and it is wholesome (nourishing), and it does away with the fatigue, and it satiates’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from abu ‘Amr from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The best of your dates is al- Barniy (a certain kind of date) which removes illnesses and there is no illness in it. It takes away fatigue, there is no harm in it, and it dissolves phlegm. With every date there is one good deed.’
In another Hadith it is said that dates give one delight, palatability, take away fatigue and satisfy one’s hunger.’”
